newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 15.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 15. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesian President Suharto said it was no use exaggerating the issue of social and economic gaps without taking any real action which can solve the problem. He said the issue of social and economic gaps will only trigger unrest.
Two companies will face court action soon for tax evasion amounting to 2.17 billion rupiah ($910,000). The companies are Graha Pasifik in East Java and Supermix Wahana Tama in East Kalimantan.

A Jakarta district court has begun the trial of a man accused of sodomising and murdering six street children. The prosecutor accused the defendant, a homeless and unemployed man, with sexually assaulting six minors aged 11 to 15 and then strangling them with plastic ropes.

Army chief of staff General Hartono said the country's largest Moslem organisation Nahdlatul Ulama (NU) was not involved in last month's riots in Tasikmalaya, West Java. A mob of mainly Moslem youth went on rampage, setting fire to shops, buildings and churches after reports of police brutality towards some Moslem leaders.

State-owned oil company Pertamina will sign a $1.13 billion loan agreement next month in Paris. The loans will be used to finance construction of Pertamina's eighth liquifed natural gas plant in Bontang, East Kalimantan.
